pairs.question: Quid facit agricola?
pairs.derivation: Augustine poses and answers his own question. Dropped the intervening framing 'interrogo uos, qui agricolae estis; quid facit agricola?' (the repeated address to the audience) and quote the single interrogative; the answer is his own reply, which ends at the full stop before 'si ergo pater deus agricola est...'.

pairs.question: Cum uenerit dominus uineae, quid faciet illis malis colonis?
pairs.answer: Malos male perdet, et uineam suam locabit aliis agricolis, qui reddant ei fructum in tempore suo.
pairs.derivation: Gospel parable quoted by Augustine. Kept 'cum uenerit dominus uineae' as setup so 'illis malis colonis' is intelligible. Stripped the framing 'responsum est:' and the editorial quotation marks; the answer ends at the full stop before 'plantata est uinea...'.

pairs.question: Quid hic statis? Quare non operamini in uinea?
pairs.derivation: The paterfamilias asks the idle workers, who reply. Stripped the speech tags 'et ait illis:' before the question and 'responderunt:' before the answer. Answer stops at the full stop before 'uenite, inquit, et uos...'.

pairs.question: Quid est, facti sunt nouissimi primi et primi nouissimi?
pairs.answer: Quia tantumdem acceperunt et primi et nouissimi.
pairs.derivation: Augustine poses and answers his own explanatory question. Clean self-contained exchange; nothing trimmed beyond it being the whole question and the whole answering clause.

pairs.question: Cuius rei finis?
pairs.derivation: Imagined dialogue with the procrastinating sinner. Stripped the framing 'respondetur tibi:' before the question and 'dicis:' before the answer. Question and answer are each quoted whole; 'iniquitatum mearum' (sc. finis) directly answers 'of what matter is it the end?'.

pairs.question: Recede a me, obsecro te, recede a me. Quare?
pairs.derivation: The lethargic sick man begs to be left alone; an interlocutor asks 'quare?' and he answers. Kept his plea 'recede a me ... recede a me' as setup so 'quare?' has a referent; stripped the framing 'inquit languidus lethargicus' from inside the plea. Answer 'dormire uolo' stops before the statement-and-retort 'sed morieris inde. ... mori uolo' which is not a Q&A.
